explanation: BKCB2 recommends $13.5M in increased funding for the Clinton Hill Brooklyn Public Library to cover forecasted needs including facade and window work, heating and cooling improvements, safety enhancements, and an interior renovation.
response: It is recommended that this request be brought to the attention of your Elected Officials.

request: Extend library hours or expand and enhance library programs
explanation: BKCB2 recommends increased funding for our 6 Brooklyn Public Library branches to 1) facilitate extended 8pm daily closures at all locations, and 2) permanent Sunday service hours at the 5 locations without: Adams Street, Center for Brooklyn History, Clinton Hill, Walt Whitman, and the Library for Arts & Culture.  Public libraries are one of our most democratizing institutions, and offer vital community services like computer and internet access, and free educational and enrichment programs for all ages. Our public libraries should be open on evenings and weekends to provide equitable access to safe and inclusive spaces for students, adults who work traditional 9-to-5 jobs, and seniors seeking community and social connection. Expanded access ensures libraries can fulfill their role as a public good accessible to all.
response: This request includes more than one proposal. The agency has recommended funding for this request in part. OMB supports the agency's position.

request: Renovate, upgrade or provide new community board facilities and equipment
explanation: BKCB2 recommends a comprehensive assessment of our operating and technical needs, and a commensurate increase in our baseline operating budget. There has been no Citywide assessment of Community Board technical needs since Windstream acquired PAETEC's municipal contracts in 2011. Windstream has consistently failed to provide reliable phone and internet service or equipment since beginning bankruptcy proceedings in 2019. This is just one example of widespread underinvestment in the basic needs of Community Board operations.  A recurring theme expressed by our City agency partners across all of this year's Borough Budget Consultations was, ""We are budgeted to address [X program/concern], but we need more support with direct local outreach."" The general public is also increasingly expectant that government offices utilize modern tools and offer digital connectivity. As the most local unit of nonpartisan City government, Community Boards need an infusion of infrastructure, equipment, and staff support to meet modern challenges, effectively partner with City agencies, efficiently serve our residents, and support greater community engagement.  The scope of assessment and investment must include basic office and field equipment updates; a survey of phone, internet, and broadcasting infrastructure and gaps; a survey of staff training and upskilling needs; and baselining of fundamental SaaS tools including design and communication (newsletter) software, and news, database, and research subscriptions.   To be clear, this requires a significant periodic investment above our extremely modest $13-$15k average annual OTPS allotment. We recommend commitment to a 4-year cycle of regular operational and technical assessments and upgrades.
response:
Agency does not support and cannot accommodate
Explanation: This is not a DCAS request.

request: Extend library hours, expand library programs, and enhance library collections
explanation: Increase Funding for New York Public Library Services in the District. In order to provide the opportunity for district children and youth to fully participate in the New York Public library's many services, funding for the Mott Haven and Woodstock branches needs to be increased to allow for all libraries to be open six days and at least forty-two hours a week. The New York Public Library and Community Board One request that the City restore funding to provide robust six day service including increased hours, diverse programming, strong collections and sufficient staff to support these functions. In these challenging economic times, the services provided through the Library are needed by New Yorkers more than ever. (Previous Tracking Codes: 101200801E)
